source: The New Humanitarian 2005 Equatorial Guinea Cholera Report
processing_notes: Source states: '946 cases and 15 deaths' in Malabo 2005 epidemic; laboratory confirmation from Pasteur Institute Yaounde Cameroon. CFR 1.6% within expected range. Only documented cholera outbreak in GNQ history. [AGENT 1 REVISION 2026-10-01] AGENT 1 VERIFICATION 2026-10-01 (article read in full via https://web.archive.org/web/20240217151550/https://www.thenewhumanitarian.org/news/2005/02/25/cholera-epidemic-kills-15-capital ; live TNH page is behind a Cloudflare challenge). Article: IRIN, DAKAR, 25 February 2005 (a Friday), 'Cholera epidemic kills 15 in capital'. Source states: 'Up to this morning, we have 15 deaths and 946 cases linked to the outbreak,' Kalula said. Source states: 'An outbreak of accute diarrhoea suspected to be cholera first appeared in Malabo, the capital of this oil-rich Central African state, two weeks ago.' Speaker: Dr Kalambay Kalula, WHO Representative in Equatorial Guinea; Pasteur Institute Yaounde confirmed all five samples as cholera; Kalula cautioned that not all those ill were necessarily cholera - interpreted as 946 sCh (suspected) and 15 deaths, cumulative for the Malabo outbreak from onset to the morning of 25 Feb 2005. PERIOD REVISED from 2005-01-01..2005-12-31 to 2005-02-10..2005-02-25 (onset 10 Feb per Cameroon Tribune 22/03/2005 citing WHO, metadata 8; consistent with 'two weeks ago'); reporting_date revised 2006-01-01 -> 2005-02-25; LOCATION revised AFR::GNQ -> AFR::GNQ::Bioko_Norte::Malabo because the source attributes the count to the Malabo outbreak (Bata's 4 confirmed January cases are a separate row). Provincial subset - do not sum with national row: WHO annual 2005 national = 6391 cases/33 deaths and JHU national 2005-02-01..2005-03-13 = 4400/30 (UID 894) are the national counts; this row is an early cumulative snapshot inside them. CONFLICT for Agent 5: JHU UID 894 gives AFR::GNQ::GQ-BN (Bioko Norte) 2005-02-01..2005-02-25 = 400 cases vs 946 here for the same place and end date. CORRECTION: the earlier note 'Only documented cholera outbreak in GNQ history' is FALSE - WHO annual reports 1984 (404/31), 1985 (108/1) and 2004 (59/1), and an unreported 1973 epidemic on Annobon (Index 8). (reason: Task D: verified IRIN/TNH article via Wayback capture 20240217151550; 946/15 is a Malabo cumulative to 25 Feb 2005, not the 2005 annual national total) [AGENT 1 REVISION 2026-10-01] CONFLICT (same date, unofficial): ASODEGUE 25 Feb 2005 (metadata 15 companion sheet, https://web.archive.org/web/20050308110526/http://www.asodegue.org:80/febrero2505.htm) reports national radio calling it 'una alarmante epidemia de colera' and that 'fuentes medicas del Hospital General de Malabo hablan de mas de 50 muertos', while authorities refused new totals; AFP 19 Feb cited anonymous hospital sources of 10-20 deaths in Malabo and Bata. WHO figure (15 deaths) retained here as the official count; unofficial figures not used. (reason: record same-date conflicting unofficial death counts for Agent 5)

source: Afrique XXI 2023 (J.-C. Servant) En Guinee equatoriale les revoltes d'Annobon
processing_notes: Source states: 'En 1973, poursuit-il, alors qu’une épidémie de choléra se propage sur l’île, le gouvernement laisse faire et n’envoie personne : 400 personnes, sur une population de 2 000 habitants, vont périr, faute de soins et de médicaments.' - interpreted as 400 deaths. Interpreted as 400 cholera deaths on Annobon (Pagalu) island in 1973; month(s) not stated so TL/TR span the calendar year. NO case count in any source - sCh left blank (deaths-only row; weekly builder skips blank-sCh rows). Speaker is historian Donato Ndongo-Bidyogo quoted by J.-C. Servant (Afrique XXI, 26 Dec 2023). CORROBORATION: (1) Republica de Annobon site (metadata 10, Level 4 advocacy) states verbatim 'La epidemia de colera de 1973 provoco la muerte de mas de 400 personas, entre ninos, mujeres y hombres' and that Macias blocked the Red Cross; (2) ICJ 1979 trial report (metadata 9, Level 2) confirms 'the population of Pagalu island (the Annoboneses) were abandoned to their fate during an epidemic of cholera' (no year/count). NOT in WHO data: Carme et al. 1983 (metadata 14) found GNQ made no official cholera notification to WHO 1970-1980, and GHO has no GNQ value before 1984 - so this is an unreported epidemic during the Macias regime, and 1970-1983 should be read as a non-reporting period, not absence. QUALITY FLAGS: round-number estimate recalled ~50 years later by a regime critic; implied mortality 400/2000 = 20% of the island population (attack rate >= 20%, far outside the 0.1-5% review band) - possible conflation with other mortality; hence confidence at the Level 3 floor (0.3). Island-only event: no national row exists for 1973; do not extrapolate to the mainland. Primary source to seek: Ndongo-Bidyogo, Historia y tragedia de Guinea Ecuatorial (1977); af Klinteberg 1978 IUEF report; Liniger-Goumaz. [AGENT 1 REVISION 2026-10-01] AGENT 1 TRIANGULATION (Batch 5): third concordant figure - CPDS La Verdad 21 Nov 2018 (metadata 18, Level 4) states verbatim 'En el ano 1973 la isla de Annobon sufre una epidemia de colera, que duro nada mas ni nada menos que tres largos meses, y durante el tiempo que la epidemia se instalo en Annobon murieron mas de 389 personas' - i.e. epidemic lasted ~3 months (months not given; TL/TR kept at full calendar year), >389 deaths. CONFLICTING FIGURES (not used): English Wikipedia 'Francisco Macias Nguema' says the 1973 epidemic resulted in 'around 100 deaths', citing Diaz Navarro I. 2015, Literaturas hispanoafricanas (Verbum) p.371 - not accessed by Agent 1; Ambo Legadu (Annobonese separatist site) claims >1,500 deaths in under six weeks and 'more than half the population' - implausible against a ~2,000 population. ASODEGUE Historia de Guinea cap. 7 (Wayback 20191027103318 of asodegue.org/hdojmc07.htm) confirms 'En 1973 se declaro una epidemia en la isla' and that Macias refused aid and barred humanitarian organisations, without naming the disease or a toll. Range of claims ~100 to >1,500; three sources converge on ~389-400; confidence kept at the Level 3 floor (0.3) because of the conflict and partisan provenance. Agent 4: seek Diaz Navarro 2015 p.371, Ndongo-Bidyogo 1977, FIDH/Thierry Mignon report (1975), af Klinteberg 1978 (IUEF). (reason: triangulation of 1973 Annobon death toll across additional sources)

Interpreted as 4 laboratory-confirmed (cCh) cholera cases in Bata (Litoral, mainland) in January 2005 ('last month' relative to the article dated 25 Feb 2005); sCh left blank because the number of suspected cases in Bata is not given (>=4). source: ASODEGUE Noticias 21 Feb 2005 (relaying AFP 17 Feb 2005) - Siete muertos por diarrea aguda en Malabo
processing_notes: Source states: '"Hemos registrado 155 casos de diarrea aguda, con y sin vómitos, de ellos han muerto tres adultos y cuatro niños" ha manifestado el director técnico del hospital de Malabo, el doctor Feliciano Panades' - interpreted as 155 sCh cases, 7 deaths. Interpreted as 155 sCh (suspected cholera: acute watery diarrhoea during the outbreak that the Pasteur Institute Yaounde confirmed as cholera on 25 Feb 2005) and 7 deaths in Malabo, cumulative to the AFP dispatch of 17 Feb 2005 (reproduced by ASODEGUE on 21 Feb 2005). At the time Dr Panades declined to call it cholera pending lab results ('Esta diarrea, que tiene los mismos sintomas que el colera, no debe todavia ser considerada como tal'); the same dispatch says >160 ill. TL 2005-02-10 = onset per Cameroon Tribune/WHO (metadata 8) and IRIN (metadata 1, 'two weeks ago' on 25 Feb); the true onset may be a few days earlier. Consistent with ASODEGUE 25 Feb 2005: authorities 'hablaban a mediados de febrero de 150 casos, de ellos siete mortales, solamente en Malabo'. Earliest dated snapshot of the 2005 epidemic: 155/7 (17 Feb) -> 946/15 WHO (25 Feb, Index 2) -> 4400/30 national (JHU UID 894, to 13 Mar) -> 6391/33 WHO annual 2005. Unofficial higher death claims recorded for Agent 5, not used: anonymous hospital sources 10-20 deaths in Malabo+Bata (AFP 19 Feb); Hospital General de Malabo sources >50 deaths (25 Feb). Provincial subset - do not sum with national row (national 2005: WHO annual 6391/33; JHU 2005-02-01..03-13 4400/30).

source: Lopez-Portoles et al. 2007 Enf Emerg 9(3):125-129 Vibrio cholerae O1 Inaba in successive cholera outbreaks Equatorial Guinea 2004-2006
processing_notes: Source states: 'El procesamiento de las correspondientes muestras de heces remitidas a los Laboratorios de Referencia de Microbiología (LRM) de los Hospitales Regionales de Bata y Malabo en los períodos en los que se produjeron dichos brotes, dio lugar al aislamiento e identificación bioquímica de 53 cepas de Vibrio cholerae procedentes de 503 coprocultivos.' - interpreted as 53 cCh confirmed cases. Interpreted as 53 laboratory-confirmed (culture) cholera cases - V. cholerae O1 serotype Inaba, ctxA-positive - among 503 acute-diarrhoea patients sampled at the Bata (Litoral) and Malabo (Bioko Norte) regional hospital reference laboratories between December 2004 and March 2006. Period from Methods: 'De diciembre de 2004 hasta marzo de 2006, fueron remitidas 503 muestras de heces'. sCh deliberately left BLANK: 503 is the number of stool samples cultured, not a case total (WHO annual 2005 alone = 6391 suspected cases), so this row must not be read as national incidence; it is a confirmed-case subset spanning two provinces (Litoral and Bioko Norte). Text also states: 'Desde finales de 2004, durante 2005 y principios de 2006 se produjeron varios picos de EDA en las ciudades de Bata y Malabo' and that the epidemic spread 'a las provincias continentales e insulares de Guinea Ecuatorial a lo largo de 16 meses'. Not additive with national counts: national 2004 = 59/1 and 2005 = 6391/33 (WHO annual, JHU UID 320) - this row is a primary count of culture-confirmed cases only, do not sum with national suspected totals. May overlap the 4 Bata confirmations of January 2005 (Index 9, Pasteur Yaounde) and the 5 Malabo samples confirmed on 25 Feb 2005. CONFLICT for Agents 3/5: cholera confirmed until early 2006 contradicts WHO-reported 2006 = 0 (JHU UID 320) and AI zero row Index 3 (2006-01-01..2010-12-31, Documented_Absence). Reporting date approximated as 2007-09-30 (issue Enf Emerg 2007;9(3)).
